title: GFS Reefer Cargo - Owner-Approved Methodology Profile
section_order: INTEREST INSURED & RELEVANT CONDITIONS OF INSURANCE POLICY
TEMPERATURE RECORDER DATA REVIEW when material
CLAIM PRESENTED ON THE POLICY & ADJUSTMENT
style_notes: Use this profile only for a current GFS-family refrigerated or frozen-cargo claim that satisfies the applicability scope; never infer the client from this profile.

Use concise numbered adjuster or surveyor notes to present the instruction, notifications, survey attendance, container examination, cargo examination, joint decisions, mitigation, delivery, and destruction events in chronological order.

Build the route from the current bill of lading and tracking evidence, keeping loading, transshipment, discharge, cross-stuffing, replacement-container movement, delivery, and inspection events distinct.

For each reefer container, keep set point, supply-air, return-air, cargo/probe readings, power events, alarm events, data gaps, and logger coverage periods separate; do not describe a set point as measured cargo temperature.
Correlate temperature changes with evidenced handling and transit events, but do not infer the timing or cause of damage from a temperature curve alone.

Record the observed container condition, power connection, seal condition, T-channel and L-plate condition, ice or blood residue, packaging, odour, leakage, discoloration, crystallisation, thawing, contamination, and sample results only when supported by current survey evidence.

Select exactly one outcome branch from current evidence: sound cargo and no claim; partial loss limited to the surveyed affected quantity; or total loss supported by rejection, health-authority, destruction, or equivalent evidence.
For a no-claim outcome, state the sound condition, accepted delivery or equivalent confirmation, and that no claim is presented; do not manufacture a cause, loss schedule, deductible, or indemnity.
For a partial loss, reconcile the initial allegation against the quantity actually surveyed or otherwise independently established and adjust only that supported quantity.
For a total loss, require evidence supporting the affected quantity, unfitness or rejection, and destruction or disposal status; do not convert deterioration language into a total loss automatically.

Test refrigeration malfunction, power interruption, temperature variation, stowage or airflow restriction, pre-shipment condition, delay, handling, and other material alternatives; identify the evidence supporting and weakening each mechanism.

Do not hold a carrier, shipper, supplier, consignee, or other party liable merely because historical reports did so; connect custody, container fitness, loading responsibility, notice, temperature records, causation, contract, and recovery economics using current evidence.

Read the current operative policy in full. Apply refrigerated-cargo clauses, packing or stowage exclusions, warranties, insurable interest, attachment, and recovery only when the current wording and facts support them; verify who packed, stowed, loaded, or instructed loading before applying a packing or stowage provision.

Calculate quantum locally from the supported affected quantity and invoice unit rate, then add only evidenced destination, customs, clearing, delivery, destruction, or other recoverable charges using the source-stated exchange rate; pending or unsupported charges remain excluded or provisional.
Preserve the source currency consistently. Flag historical or current-document currency, commodity, quantity, rate, total, or arithmetic inconsistencies instead of copying them into the report.

Use representative current-claim inspection, cross-stuffing, mitigation, and destruction photographs under the global Appendix limits; historical photographs and filenames are never reusable claim evidence.

The global ULA report specification, Director wording, no-fabrication rules, deterministic calculations, citation requirements, empty Enclosure and Outstanding sections, and human approval gates take precedence over any inconsistent wording found in a historical GFS report.
